- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/26 (Fri) 01:40
- [FACT] User is considering going back to school for a graduate degree.
- [USER_SAID] User asked about the benefits of having a master's degree in terms of career advancement and salary increase.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pursuing a master's degree can enhance credibility and recognition, access to senior roles, specialization and expertise, networking opportunities, and help in staying competitive.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Higher earning potential for master's degree holders is about 20% higher than those with a bachelor's degree.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Salary premium for master's degree holders can be around 10-20% compared to those with a bachelor's degree in the same field.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of salary increases by field include: MBA (20-50%), Engineering (15-30%), Computer Science (20-40%), Healthcare Administration (15-30%), Education (10-20%).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional considerations include Return on Investment (ROI) and personal fulfillment.
- [USER_SAID] User requested recommendations for online resources or websites that provide information on graduate programs and their ROI.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended resources include GradSchools.com, Peterson's, GraduateGuide.com, PayScale's Graduate School ROI Report, NerdWallet's Graduate Degree ROI Calculator, Forbes' Best Master's Degrees for Jobs, US News & World Report's Best Graduate Schools, The Princeton Review's Graduate School Rankings, Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), Glassdoor, LinkedIn's Salary Tool, Reddit's r/gradschool, GradCafe, and The Grad Student Forum.
- [USER_SAID] User asked for recommendations for online courses or certification programs to upskill and reskill in their current field without committing to a full graduate degree.
